symptom:
`src/oidc/jwks.zig` contains at least four hard Zig 0.16 compile errors, yet `zig build` and `zig build test` both exit 0. Verified empirically by rooting a throwaway test at src/ that imports the module and calls `initCache`/`deinitCache`:
  - src/oidc/jwks.zig:322  `var cache_mutex: std.Thread.Mutex = .{};` — `std.Thread` has no member `Mutex` in Zig 0.16 (it moved to `std.Io.Mutex`, whose lock/unlock additionally take an `Io` parameter, so this is not a rename-only fix).
  - src/oidc/jwks.zig:140  `std.ArrayList(TokenCacheKey).init(self.allocator)` — `std.ArrayList(T)` has no `init` in Zig 0.16.
  - src/oidc/jwks.zig:239  `std.ArrayList(DenylistEntry).init(allocator)` — same.
  - src/oidc/jwks.zig:248  `self.entries.deinit()` — `deinit` now requires the allocator argument.
The file is exported from `src/main.zig:78` (`pub const oidc_jwks = @import("oidc/jwks.zig");`), so it LOOKS wired.
root_cause: Exactly the ISS-0172 / GH #500 blind spot, in a second subsystem. `src/main.zig` re-exports the module, but nothing calls `initCache`, `deinitCache`, or any other function in it, and nothing instantiates the module-level `var`s. Zig resolves a top-level `var`'s type lazily and does not semantically analyse a function body that is never referenced, so neither the stale `std.Thread.Mutex` declaration nor the stale ArrayList call sites are ever reported. A plain `@import` re-export is NOT proof that a file compiles.
acceptance_criteria: src/oidc/jwks.zig compiles under Zig 0.16: the mutex is replaced with a primitive usable from its call sites (std.Io.Mutex requires an Io parameter at lock/unlock, so the call sites must thread one through or the design must change), and every std.ArrayList(T).init / .deinit() call site is migrated to the 0.16 API.
A build target genuinely ANALYSES the file — a test that calls initCache/deinitCache and exercises TokenValidationCache and JtiDenylist, not a bare `_ = oidc_jwks;` pin (see ISS-0172).
Deliberate-mutation verification: inject a statement error into a jwks.zig function body and confirm the target goes red.
The ISS-402 OIDC token validation cache behaviour (GH #198) is re-verified once the file actually compiles — its tests have never run.
A census is run for the same pattern: every `pub const X = @import(...)` in src/main.zig / src/bpm.zig whose module has no reachable caller.
notes: Filed and forwarded per CLAUDE.md 'Unblock-Everything' scope boundary and docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md. It does NOT block ISS-0169 tranche 1: nothing in src/lua/ imports src/oidc/jwks.zig, and `zig build`, `zig build test` and `zig build test-lua` are all green on the WF03-ISS-0169-20260806 branch.

Noticed while fixing the IDENTICAL stale `std.Thread.Mutex` spelling in src/lua/memory_limiter.zig (ISS-0169 diagnosis E4), which the ISS-0169 diagnosis had already flagged as 'whether that file is analysed was not determined here'. This issue determines it: it is not.
Security-relevant: this is the OIDC token validation cache and the JTI replay denylist. Code that has never been compiled cannot be assumed to enforce a replay defence.

Reproduce: create src/jwks_probe_root.zig containing `const jwks = @import("oidc/jwks.zig"); test { try jwks.initCache(std.testing.allocator); jwks.deinitCache(); }` and run `zig test src/jwks_probe_root.zig`.
